Data warehouse company MotherDuck has acquired Tower Computing Inc., a startup that was already running the infrastructure behind MotherDuck's AI-generated data pipelines, according to [MotherDuck's announcement](https://motherduck.com/blog/motherduck-acquires-tower/). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis) at 567 words, within the 400-1200 word range for the News category. Neutral, factual prose with attribution on every sentence carrying a specific claim.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both source snapshots in full after verifying sha256 integrity against manifest.json (both matched; both fetched with status_code 200, no archive_fallback, no suspicious_patterns). source-0.html.gz (motherduck.com/blog/motherduck-acquires-tower/, MotherDuck's own announcement, posted by Jordan Tigani, dated 2026/08/25): confirms the acquisition of 'Tower Computing Inc.', the framing that Tower already powered MotherDuck Flights, the quote 'the sandboxing, scheduling, and observability' as the functionality Tower supplied, the verbatim quote 'in only a matter of weeks without compromising on features like observability and reliability', and the Data-APIs/Dives pairing described in the article. source-1.html.gz (thenewstack.io/motherduck-tower-acquisition-python/, Paul Sawers, dated Aug 25 2026): confirms MotherDuck founded 2022 by Jordan Tigani ('a former engineering lead at Google focused on BigQuery'), ~$100M raised since inception, Tower founded late 2024 by ex-Snowflake engineers Serhii Sokolenko (CEO) and Brad Heller (CTO), Tower as a managed Python-pipeline runtime, the Flights feature and its June 2026 launch, the plan to eventually merge Flights with Ducklings, the Tower Control agent description, and the Databricks Genie Code / Snowflake CoCo and CoCo Automations comparisons. Both quotes attributed to Tigani ('We became their largest customer almost overnight, and our teams have been shipping together ever since'; 'There's a rule I've relearned at every infrastructure company I've worked at: you can rent a feature, but you can't rent a foundation'; 'when an agent inside MotherDuck builds a job and schedules it, the thing executing that job is our product — whatever logo is on it') and the Sokolenko quote ('Joining a hyperscaler usually means adapting to its legacy architecture') were each checked character-for-character against the New Stack transcript and match verbatim, with correct speaker attribution. Neither source discloses financial terms of the deal; the article's 'What We Don't Know' section correctly reports the terms as undisclosed rather than inventing a figure.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinated or fabricated specifics found. Every number, name, date, and quote in the body traces to one of the two cited sources. The one automated finding — motherduck.com not present in config/source_allowlist.txt — is an allowlist-curation gap, not a factual-accuracy problem: it is the acquiring company's own official blog, used only to source claims about its own acquisition and product plans, which is standard and appropriate use of a primary source. Per established precedent in this newsroom (e.g. the 2026-08-11 Bank of America/EricaAssist review, which approved outright despite an identical 'not in allowlist' warning against newsroom.bankofamerica.com), a first-party corporate announcement used for facts about that company's own action does not require a public corrections record; it is noted here and the allowlist recommendation is passed along for the maintainers.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing beyond the clearly-labeled Analysis section, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. Checked src/content/articles/2026-08/ for MotherDuck/Tower coverage: none exists. The only prior DuckDB-ecosystem articles this month are 2026-08-20 (DuckDB v2.0 'Cyanoptera' preview) and 2026-08-26 (AWS's agreement to acquire DuckLabs). Read the AWS/DuckLabs article in full: it covers Amazon's definitive agreement to acquire DuckLabs — the Amsterdam company behind the open-source DuckDB engine, founded by Hannes Muhleisen and Mark Raasveldt — an entirely different acquirer, target, and set of people from MotherDuck buying Tower Computing Inc. (a Python-pipeline-runtime startup founded by Serhii Sokolenko and Brad Heller). The submission's own Analysis section explicitly and correctly distinguishes the two deals ('a separate transaction with a different acquirer and a different target'), which I independently verified is accurate — this is not a confusion or conflation of the two stories. PR #2297 (mold linker) is unrelated to this topic and not a duplicate concern.
concerns: motherduck.com is not yet in config/source_allowlist.txt; recommend the site maintainers add it given it is a legitimate, frequently-citable primary source for MotherDuck's own product/company announcements.
recommendations: Add motherduck.com to config/source_allowlist.txt so future submissions citing MotherDuck's own blog do not repeatedly trip this warning.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality, accurately sourced submission. Both direct quotes from Tigani and Sokolenko verified verbatim against the New Stack snapshot with correct attribution; deal terms correctly reported as undisclosed; the article's own Analysis section correctly and independently distinguishes this deal from the unrelated, already-published AWS/DuckLabs acquisition. Approved without corrections.
